decisions.reason: After two years this recruitment service remains far from the firm's maritime core and strategic path, so its limited synergies and weaker option value no longer justify keeping resources tied up.
The maritime education programme fits the firm's existing training capabilities and partner network, and its early expansion to six institutions suggests useful upside with low abandonment pressure.

Emissions monitoring and compliance services are close to the core offer, backed by a clear regulatory need and an early execution success across all relevant vessels, so the option should be retained.
The emissions compliance dashboard supports the firm's digitalisation direction and is integrated into its ship management software, but as a newer tool its commercial value is still being tested.

The emissions compliance cost simulation tool is strategically related and digitally embedded, yet as an early-stage analytical add-on it still carries somewhat more uncertainty than the broader compliance service.
